chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Al-Qandi, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Fever was mentioned to him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'We, the People of the Household, do not cure it except by pouring cold water upon us and eating apples.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended treatment for fever according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the Ahl al-Bayt’s medical practice of using cold water and apples for fever to their spiritual lineage, emphasizing the integration of physical health with divine tradition. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imams possess both spiritual authority and practical wisdom in medicine, often prescribing simple, natural remedies rooted in Sunnah. The mention of apples specifically connects to broader Islamic traditions regarding the fruit's medicinal and spiritual benefits.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companioins, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Al Qindy, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

The fever was mentioned to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household do not cure it except by the pouring of the cold water upon us (for cooling the external heat) and eating the apple (for cooling the internal heat)’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad Ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from al-Qandiy from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following: “

Once, fever was mentioned before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘We are the people of the family who do not use any medicine for it except pouring cold water on us and eating apples.’”
